name: Hag, Hearth
body:
HEARTH HAG
CR 5

This stooped figure leans on her broom, smelling of pungent ash and alchemical ingredients.

XP 1,600
LE Medium monstrous humanoid
Init –1; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +11

DEFENSE

AC 17, touch 9, flat-footed 17 (+4 armor, -1 Dex, +4 natural)
hp 57 (6d10+24)
Fort +8, Ref +4, Will +7; Resist cold 10, fire 10; SR 17

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee broom +11/+6 (1d6+4 plus 1d6 fire)
Special Attacks cleaning strike
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 6th; concentration +9)

Constant—mage armor
At will—detect chaos, detect magic
1/day—alarm, arcane lock, burning hands (DC 14), cure disease, cure serious wounds, lesser geas, glyph of warding, neutralize poison, remove curse

STATISTICS

Str 17, Dex 8, Con 16, Int 11, Wis 14, Cha 17
Base Atk +6; CMB +9; CMD 18
Feats Catch Off-Guard, Iron Will, Toughness
Skills Heal +8, Craft (alchemy) +8, Knowledge (local) +6, Perception +11
Languages Common, Giant
SQ hearth broom

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Cleansing Strike (Su)

When the hearth hag uses the attack action to take a single attack with her broom and hits with that attack, she may remove effects from that creature as a targeted dispel magic.

Hearth Broom (Su)

In a hearth hag’s hands, her broom is an improvised weapon that counts as a +1 flaming club. She is proficient with its use due to the Catch Off-Guard feat.

ECOLOGY

Environment any cold
Organization solitary, family (1 plus 2–8 changeling witches), or coven (3 hags of any type)
Treasure standard plus broom

Hearth hags are more social than their kin, living near humanoid settlements and trading their services for the offspring of that community. Many settlements drive off hearth hags, but others consider hags’ power worth the difficult cost.

The hearth hags see themselves as providing valuable services for their communities and rescuing children from those who would neglect them. In some cases, these rationalizations are actually the truth. But most hearth hags enjoy driving a hard bargain, making harsh demands of the desperate and using their changeling daughters as slave labor.

A coven including a hearth hag adds mage’s magnificent mansion and wall of stone instead of blight and force cage.
